acceptance_criteria.description: Windows ACL identity and verification scripts resolve Microsoft.PowerShell.Security from the absolute SystemRoot Windows PowerShell module directory, never from ambient PowerShell Core or user module paths.
The injected-runner test proves the bounded PSModulePath, and the native current-host owner-only test passes.
Focused artifact permission tests, lint, and typecheck pass without weakening ACL verification or shell isolation.

closed_decisions: The failure is a module-shadowing collision: the inherited PSModulePath exposes a PowerShell Core Microsoft.PowerShell.Security module before the Windows PowerShell module.
Use only the absolute SystemRoot WindowsPowerShell v1.0 Modules directory for the child PSModulePath; do not import ambient user, project, cache, or PowerShell Core modules.
Keep powershell.exe and icacls.exe absolute, shell false, current-SID ownership, protected ACL, one-rule, and full-control verification unchanged.
